newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish insurer PZU's 1996 loss bigger after audit.
newsitem.headline: Polish insurer PZU's 1996 loss bigger after audit.

text.p: Poland's largest insurance firm Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU) had a higher 1996 net loss than the earlier reported 92 million zlotys, the company's spokesman said on Monday.
Marek Maszek told Reuters the loss was bigger because the firm's auditor KPMG demanded increasing technical reserves.
"After audit it turned out that the loss is bigger than we assumed, which is due to provisions...the auditor demanded to increase them," he said.
He declined to give any figures and added the final results should be published after the company's supervisory board meeting in the second half of the month.
On Saturday Gazeta Wyborcza reported that PZU had a net loss of 170 million zlotys.
PZU had a net profit of 205 million zlotys in the first quarter of 1997, against a 57-million-zloty loss in 1996 in the same period.
